title: analyzing-opencode-usage Change Request and Planning
outcome: Wrote comprehensive change request specification covering 12 bugs, 5 new metric requirements, 5 refactoring tasks, and 4 implementation phases. Consulted world-review for analysis on token efficiency metrics and prioritization.
key_decisions: Structured change request in 4 parts: bugs, new metrics, refactoring, implementation phases
Proposed 7 novel efficiency metrics: context-to-output ratio, zero-change rate, cache efficiency trend, token density, agent overlap, session complexity, refinement loops
Identified 6 open questions for discussion before planning begins
Phased implementation: bug fixes first (prerequisites), then core metrics, then advanced attribution
learnings: The 3D model×agent×day breakdown doesn't exist — cross_tab has model×agent totals, timeseries has per-day by category only
Cost calculation has two inconsistent methods (flat rates vs per-model rates) producing $10 discrepancy
Session purpose (feature vs bugfix) is not trackable without either commit message parsing or new data collection
world-review subagent provided thorough analysis but general subagent was more reliable for code review
next_steps: Discuss open questions with user (session purpose tagging, per-commit attribution, custom model pricing, path aliases, metric priority, cost display)
Plan Phase 2 core new metrics (model×agent×day, per-model daily cost, novel efficiency metrics)
